'''Indian Railway Finance Corporation''' (IRFC) is an Indian [[public sector undertaking]] (PSU)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-01-31/news/36658972_1_irfc-bonds-tax-free-bonds-tenure-bonds|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410133317/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-01-31/news/36658972_1_irfc-bonds-tax-free-bonds-tenure-bonds|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 April 2015|title=IRFC, HUDCO tax free bonds closing date entended, should you invest?|work=Economic Times }}</ref> engaged in raising financial resources for expansion and running through capital markets and other borrowings.<ref>{{cite web |title=IRFC Rides High: Rail PSU Stock Soars 12% This Week, Analysts Eye Further Upside |url=https://www.brutimes.com/news/business/irfc-rides-high-rail-psu-stock-soars-12-this-week-analysts-eye-further-upside |website=Bru Times News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-02-24/news/37270173_1_tax-free-bonds-irfc-iifcl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150409022016/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-02-24/news/37270173_1_tax-free-bonds-irfc-iifcl|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 April 2015|title=IRFC, Rural Electrification Corp, IIFC eye Rs 12,000 crore through tax-free bonds|work=Economic Times }}</ref> The [[Government of India]] owns a majority stake in the company, while the [[Ministry of Railways (India)|Ministry of Railways]] has administrative control.<ref name="Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna CPSEs">{{cite web |title=Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna CPSEs |url=https://dpe.gov.in/maharatna-navratna-and-miniratna-cpses |website=dpe.gov.in |publisher=Department of Public Enterprises (Indian Government) |access-date=28 September 2021}}</ref> In March 2025, IRFC was given the [[Public Sector Undertakings in India#List of Navratna|Navaratna]] status by the Government of India, becoming the 26th PSU in this list.<ref>{{cite news |title=IRCTC, IRFC get 'navratna' status. What does it mean for the two railway PSUs? |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/irctc-irfc-get-navratna-status-what-does-it-mean-for-the-two-railway-psus-11740996086491.html |access-date=14 March 2025 |work=Livemint |date=3 March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date= |title=IRCTC receives Maharatna Tag |url=https://x.com/DPE_GoI/status/1896488580756701191?t=E-QpL4hFfGYkMwfKUQahmw&s=19 |access-date= |work=Twitter}}</ref>

==History==
IRFC was founded on 12 December 1986.<ref name="The Hans India">{{cite news |last1=Jha |first1=J. K. |title=Indian Railway Finance Corporation IPO: Opens tomorrow: Key details an investor should know before subscribing |url=https://www.thehansindia.com/business/indian-railway-finance-corporation-ipo-opens-tomorrow-key-details-an-investor-should-know-before-subscribing-667190 |date=17 January 2021 |access-date=11 September 2021 |work=www.thehansindia.com |language=en}}</ref> It started borrowing from the market in 1987–88.

The company launched its [[initial public offering]] on 18 January 2021<ref name="NDTV IRFC IPO">{{cite news |title=IRFC IPO: First IPO Of 2021 To Open On January 18: Key Things To Know |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/irfc-ipo-indian-railways-finance-corporation-ipo-opens-january-18-check-price-band-grey-market-premium-2351893 |access-date=2 August 2021 |work=NDTV.com |date=13 January 2021}}</ref> and got listed on the [[National Stock Exchange of India]] and [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] on 29 January 2021.

As of 2024-25 Q3 reports, its promoter group (Government of India) holds 86.36% ownership while the public has the rest of the 13.64% shares.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shareholding Pattern FY 2024-25 Q3 |url=https://irfc.co.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Shareholding%20Pattern%20FY%202024-25%20Q3.pdf |website=irfc.co.in |publisher=IRFC |access-date=14 March 2025}}</ref> In January 2026, Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) reported its highest ever quarterly profit for the third straight quarter, driven by steady loan growth and better margins. Profit after tax for the December 2025 quarter rose 11% YoY to Rs 1,802 crore.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Podishetti |first=Akash |date=2026-01-19 |title=IRFC Q3 Results: Co posts its biggest-ever profit of Rs 1,802 crore, up 11% YoY |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/earnings/irfc-q3-results-co-posts-its-biggest-ever-profit-of-rs-1802-crore-up-11-yoy/articleshow/126674298.cms?utm_ |access-date=2026-01-19 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

==Operations==
IRFC raises money through financial bonds and from banks and financial institutions.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/Select-institutions-can-raise-Rs-50000-cr-tax-free-bonds/article20584940.ece | title=Select institutions can raise Rs 50,000 cr tax-free bonds | date=28 February 2013 | newspaper=The Hindu Business Line | access-date=7 July 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title=LIC will invest up to Rs 26,000 crore in IRFC | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/lic-will-invest-up-to-rs-26000-crore-in-irfc/articleshow/64864973.cms | first=Saikat | last=Das | newspaper=The Economic Times | date=5 July 2018 | access-date=6 November 2020 }}</ref>

==Board of directors==
IRFC's Board of Directors includes Uma Ranade as chairman and managing director, Shelly Verma as Director (Finance), Baldeo Purushartha as Nominee Director, [[Vallabhbhai Maneklal Patel]] as Non-Official Independent Director, and Sheela Pandit as Non-Official Independent Director.<ref>{{cite web|title=IRFC Board of Directors|url=https://irfc.co.in/board-of-directors/|access-date=12 August 2022|archive-date=12 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812045040/https://irfc.co.in/board-of-directors/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="TribuneNews AB">{{cite news |title=Amitabh Banerjee appointed managing director of IRFC |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/business/amitabh-banerjee-appointed-managing-director-of-irfc-853125 |access-date=7 September 2021 |work=Tribuneindia News Service |language=en}}</ref>

extract: Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is an Indian public sector undertaking (PSU) engaged in raising financial resources for expansion and running through capital markets and other borrowings. The Government of India owns a majority stake in the company, while the Ministry of Railways has administrative control. In March 2025, IRFC was given the Navaratna status by the Government of India, becoming the 26th PSU in this list.
